title: My pixel canvas game became unplayable with 100 players. AI helped me rebuild it from scratch in Rust, and it now handles 5,000
author: gaspasho
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev, solo dev from France here.

PixelVerse is an infinite shared canvas, a bit like r/place but with no edges and no reset. Players place colors and Unicode characters on a world that keeps growing.

The first version ran on Firebase, and with about 100 people drawing at once the game became unplayable. So I started over from zero, with coding agents: a Rust server with WebSockets, the live world kept in memory, SQLite, all on one small VPS.

Measured in production on 2 CPUs and 3.7 GB of RAM:  
\- 5,000 concurrent players, with 95% of actions answered in under 7 ms  
\- around 10,000 spectators before the CPU tops out

I think this is where AI can really help solo game developers: keeping a game's running costs under control. With AI, I got 50x more players on the server for half the price.

Two weeks, 460+ issues and PRs, about 22k lines of Rust.  
You can explore the canvas without an account. Happy to answer questions.

[https://pixelverse.fr/en](https://pixelverse.fr/en?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=aigamedev)
